@GadflyQuebec @Roscoe1945 @pelchat_gerald @GasPriceWizard @GregSweet11 You are completely winging it now. All QC has is massive hydro resources, and it imports oil from areas outside Canada, with no env. Controls or carbon taxes, and slams the west for our resources, while getting a free ride on cement. You are a hypocrite in a free ride province.

@CooperLorne @Roscoe1945 @pelchat_gerald @GasPriceWizard @GregSweet11 most industries, an active agency that evaluates new projects, and a climate plan that will cut emissions 37.5% by 2030. And the fight continues to make Quebec do even better. Montreal's aiming at 55%.

@GadflyQuebec @CooperLorne @pelchat_gerald @GasPriceWizard @GregSweet11 No one is hitting their targets for good reason. Oddly the Liberals adopted the Conservative targets in 2015 and somehow PQ is exempt from the new carbon tax I believe.

@Roscoe1945 @CooperLorne @pelchat_gerald @GasPriceWizard @GregSweet11 Frankly, I'm furious that the Liberals kept Harper's weak climate targets. I'm not happy that other countries missed their targets, either. But at last we do have some kind of federal plan, flawed though it may be, & other countries are stepping up efforts.

@Roscoe1945 @CooperLorne @pelchat_gerald @GasPriceWizard @GregSweet11 The reason Quebec (& BC) aren't affected by the federal carbon price is because we've been using cap-and-trade with California for ages to cut our emissions. The provinces affected are those that didn't implement their own plans; if they would, they'd be exempted too.

@GadflyQuebec @CooperLorne @pelchat_gerald @GasPriceWizard @GregSweet11 You know that’s a good point but I’ve never really seen any black and white data how it works. And why California? I’d like to see how it works. If we’re all in this together as a country than it should all be as such.

@Roscoe1945 @CooperLorne @pelchat_gerald @GasPriceWizard @GregSweet11 California because, like BC & QC, they've got a lot of "green" taxpayers pressing for climate action since the 1960s. Haven't got the numbers but the principle is there's a ceiling on GHG emissions—that's supposed to get lower over time—but a low-emissions company can sell its…

@GadflyQuebec @Roscoe1945 @CooperLorne @pelchat_gerald @GasPriceWizard @GregSweet11 BC is not on a “cap and trade” system with California.

BC has a carbon tax which was instituted against the wishes of the majority of the province, is a straight cash grab and does not result in any “reduction in emissions”.  It does result in significant tax collection.
@Guinness_kel @Roscoe1945 @CooperLorne @pelchat_gerald @GasPriceWizard @GregSweet11 Sorry: it seems I'm out of date on BC. Originally they were supposed to be in the cap-&-trade camp.
